title: Throughput contract verification harness and customer onboarding checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a verification harness and standardized customer acceptance checklist to validate dedicated capacity throughput contracts. The goal is to provide reproducible tests and decision criteria that prove a customer's committed pool meets latency and tokens/sec guarantees under realistic workload mixes and failure modes. This ticket covers harness infra, statistical pass/fail rules, replayable traffic capture, autoscaling policy effects, and a one-page onboarding checklist for Solutions / CSMs.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible load harness that can run stable experiments against Dedicated GPU pools and produce an HTML summary report
Statistical pass/fail rules defined (p99/p95/TPS with 95% confidence) documented in the methodology doc
Traffic capture and deterministic replay tool available and used in at least 3 customer validation runs
Runbook for running customer acceptance test with clear failure modes and mitigation steps
Onboarding checklist (one-pager) created and reviewed by Solutions, SRE, and PM
Automated dashboard report (Grafana) that maps run results to SLA contract fields
tasks: Design experiment methodology and statistical rules (PRD: confluence: /display/INF/Throughput+Contract+Methodology)
Implement harness CLI that can produce client-side traffic shapes (steady, burst, diurnal, tail-heavy)
Add deterministic traffic recording and replay module that includes KV-cache warmup scenarios
Integrate harness with infra orchestration to pin model variant, quantization profile, and routing policy
Create HTML summary generator and Grafana dashboard panels for token/sec, p50/p95/p99, error rate
Run three internal validation runs across different fleet sizes and capture learnings
Publish customer onboarding checklist and runbook and conduct dry-run with Solutions team
recent_updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Solutions, and Product. Agreed high-level SLAs to validate: tokens/sec and tail latency budget per model class.
2025-01-22: Prototype harness v0.1 submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-harness/pull/17 (initial traffic shapes and reporter)
2025-01-30: Decided to use bootstrap confidence intervals over single-run thresholds to reduce false positives in noisy environments.
2025-02-05: Added deterministic replay to account for KV cache warmup; found 12% throughput delta between warm and cold runs on rtx-a100-80gb pools.
2025-02-12: Draft onboarding checklist reviewed by CSMs; feedback: include clear escalation contact and expected artifacts to attach (run-id, grafana link, PR results).
2025-02-18: Internal validation #2 failed due to autoscaler misconfiguration; filed ENG-48255 to fix policy interpolation bug. Reran after fix and succeeded.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use bootstrap CIs vs parametric tests: protects against non-normal latency distributions seen in production at high concurrency.
Prefer deterministic replay of recorded traffic rather than purely synthetic generators to capture real prompt length and KV-cache patterns.
Keep harness language-agnostic but ship with Python and Go clients; Solutions team preferred Python for on-prem runs.
Do not attempt to fully emulate cross-customer multi-tenant noise in initial phase; instead document limitations and add 'noisy neighbor' optional test for Phase 2.
risks: False pass due to inadequate cache-warmup handling - mitigated by replay warmup phase
Cluster autoscaler behavior can mask regressions if not pinned during test - mitigated by control flags in harness
Customer expectations may overfit to synthetic workload - mitigated by recommending recorded-replay runs for each customer
Long-running experiments consume capacity in prod-like environments - mitigated by scheduling windows and quota controls
